transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time. I'm sure it's mostly just stress—I'm a chief executive, so there's always a lot of pressure, you know? But I wanted to be proactive and make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in. 

I'm here because... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, and I really don't want you to think badly of me. But I keep hearing people talking about me. It usually happens through the conference room walls at work, or... or even coming from my phone when it's completely turned off. It’s usually the board members or my staff, and they’re saying that I’m ruining the company. Which I'm not, I promise I'm actually doing a really good job. 

It's just... it sounds so perfectly clear that I actually catch myself answering them out loud before I realize that no one else around me heard anything. 

I know that probably sounds a bit strange. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been hearing these voices talking about you — days, weeks, or longer?

Um... well, it definitely hasn't been forever, I promise. I always try to handle things on my own, so I kept thinking it would just go away if I got a little more sleep or managed my schedule better. 

But I guess... if I really think about it, the voices from the walls and my phone have been happening for about the past three months. 

I know I probably should have called you sooner, and I'm really sorry if I let it go on too long before asking for help. I just didn't want to overreact. Is three months... does that sound like a normal amount of time for a severe stress reaction? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details so I can be a good patient for you.

During these past three months, have you also noticed any changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or empty, or on the other hand, unusually elevated, euphoric, or needing much less sleep than normal?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I try really hard to maintain a good attitude, especially for my team. I definitely haven't felt sad or... or empty. I love my company too much for that, and I try to always look on the bright side of things. 

And I haven't been unusually elevated or anything like that either. I'm sleeping my regular amount—well, as much as any executive does, anyway, but I'm certainly not skipping sleep or feeling like I don't need it. I know how important rest is, so I try to be really responsible about that.

I always try to stay very level-headed. I really don't want you to think I'm unstable or overly emotional. I hope that's a good sign? That my mood is mostly just... normal? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need. Am I doing okay so far?

Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications, or do you have any medical conditions like thyroid problems, seizures, or a head injury, that started around the same time as these voices?

Oh, goodness, no. I promise I would never do anything like... like recreational drugs. I take my position at the company very seriously, so I always make sure to keep a clear head. Um, I might have a single glass of wine at a networking dinner every now and then, but that's absolutely it, I swear. 

And I'm not taking any new medications at all. As for the medical things you mentioned... no, no head injuries or seizures, and my thyroid is perfectly fine. I'm actually very diligent about getting my annual physicals. I always want to make sure I'm in top shape so I don't let my team down. 

I really hope that helps rule some things out? I just want you to know I haven't been doing anything irresponsible that would have caused this. Did I answer all the parts of your question okay?

Since these experiences started about three months ago, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to function at work or in your personal life—things like difficulty concentrating, getting tasks done, or keeping up with your usual routine?

Um... well... I want to be completely honest with you, because I know you need the truth to help me. But... it's a little hard to admit. I've always prided myself on being the one who holds everything together. 

But, um... lately, I guess things have slipped a little bit. Just a little. I mean, I'm still going to work every day! But... I'm not really running my division the way I usually do. Some of the executive decisions... I've been having a hard time keeping up with them. My senior staff—they're so wonderful, really—they've sort of quietly stepped in to handle some of the things I used to do myself. I didn't ask them to, but I think they noticed I was struggling to concentrate with... with the voices. 

And at home... oh, I feel so terrible about this... my husband has really had to take over almost everything. I start things and just... leave them unfinished, or I can't even bring myself to start them at all. I feel like such a burden to him, even though he says it's fine. 

I'm really trying my best to push through it, I promise. I don't want to sound like I'm just giving up or being lazy. Is it... is it normal for stress to make it this hard to just do my normal routine? I hope I'm not disappointing you by not handling things better.

Have you noticed any changes in how you express your emotions, your motivation to do things you used to enjoy, or in how your thoughts or speech come out—like others telling you your thinking seems jumbled or hard to follow?

Um... well... I hope you won't think less of me for this. I really do try to be upbeat, I promise. But... I suppose things have changed a little bit in that way, too. 

I used to be the person driving every single idea, you know? I'd be calling people after openings, getting everyone excited... I was always so passionate. But lately... um... I can just sit at my desk for hours, just staring at the agenda. I don't really know where the time goes. And I feel so guilty about it, but I barely speak to my staff anymore. Or even my husband. I just... I don't have the energy to talk. 

And the worst part—and please don't think I'm a bad person for this—is that I just feel... almost nothing about the work I used to absolutely love. It's like my emotions are just sort of... flat? 

As for my thoughts being jumbled... I don't think I'm hard to follow, am I? I really try to speak clearly for you. I hope my answers make sense. I'm just trying to be as helpful as I can, even though it's hard to admit I'm not my usual self right now. Am I explaining things okay?

I think... well, it's been building up for about two years and four months now. It started right around the time of the big company expansion, when they put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division. I was so honored they trusted me with it, I really was! But... I guess that's when I first started noticing the changes. I just didn't want to admit it to anyone because I didn't want them to think I couldn't handle the promotion. 

I'm so sorry if I should have mentioned that sooner. I just... I wanted to believe it was just a temporary thing, you know? I hope that timeline makes sense to you? I'm really trying to give you the exact right information so you can help me. Did I explain that okay?
